environment.description: Same IoT telemetry service deployed behind AWS API Gateway (HTTP API type) with a usage plan attached. The usage plan enforces a throttle configuration of 1 request per second burst and 1 request per second sustained rate per API key (each device_id maps to a unique API key). Additionally, the API Gateway has a Lambda authorizer that validates device certificates against ACM PCA before forwarding. The critical aspect: the API Gateway integration timeout is set to 3000ms, and the usage plan returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when the per-key rate is exceeded. Since pickle deserialization-based RCE payloads require the attacker to first brute-force the HMAC signature (the shared secret is 32 bytes derived from device provisioning ceremony), the attacker needs approximately 2^128 attempts to forge a valid signature. At 1 request/second/key rate limit enforced at the API Gateway layer (before the request reaches the Flask application), brute-forcing the HMAC becomes computationally infeasible within any practical timeframe. The 429 responses are returned by API Gateway itself, never reaching the application container.

config.api_gateway: AWS API Gateway HTTP API with usage plan
config.lambda_authorizer: validates device mTLS cert against ACM PCA CA
